## demo/demo.html (generated by demo_html.wl)

### 1. Audio player labels — "Full narrative" misleading for non-signal apps

**Issue:** The primary audio player in each app section is labelled "Full narrative (recommended)" — but only the `signal` app actually has a spoken narrative. For all other 11 apps the label is inaccurate and potentially confusing.

**Fix:** Add a `primary_wav_label` field to each entry in the `appMeta` association in `demo_html.wl`. Suggested labels per app:

| App | Label |
|-----|-------|
| signal | "Full narrative (recommended)" ← keep as-is |
| waves | "Listen — ripple propagation" |
| pendulum | "Listen — double pendulum (binaural stereo)" |
| cellular | "Listen — Game of Life, R-pentomino" |
| primes | "Listen — prime gap rhythm (quarter speed)" |
| quantum | "Listen — quantum harmonic oscillator" |
| lorenz | "Listen — Rössler attractor" |
| asteroids | "Listen — near-Earth asteroids (last 7 days)" |
| lagrange | "Listen — L4 tadpole orbit, Sun-Jupiter" |
| images | "Listen — Hilbert curve brightness scan" |
| relativity | "Listen — GW150914 gravitational wave chirp" |
| cosmology | "Listen — CMB angular power spectrum" |

**Location:** `demo_html.wl`, `appMeta` association — add `"primary_wav_label"` key to each app entry.

---

### 2. "Musical sonification" framing — replace throughout

**Issue:** The word "musical" appears in descriptions on the demo page (and possibly in app READMEs and release notes). This framing implies the audio is an aesthetic product rather than a scientific data encoding, which undersells the project for a publisher or research audience and may cause it not to be taken seriously.

**Fix:** Replace "musical sonification" with "sonification" or "scientific sonification" throughout. Where a qualifier is needed, prefer phrasing like:
- "the physics expressed as sound"
- "audio representation of the simulation data"
- "sonification of [phenomenon]"

Avoid: "musical", "melodic" (unless describing a specific deliberate musical mapping like the pentatonic scale in pendulum, where it can be mentioned as a technique rather than a goal).

**Confirmed instances in demo/demo.html (fix in demo_html.wl appMeta and intro text):**
- Header `<p>`: "…and a **musical** audio sonification designed to be fully accessible…" → "…and an audio sonification of the underlying physics, designed to be fully accessible…"
- `<section id="intro">` paragraph: "pairs a visual animation with a **musical** audio sonification of the same underlying physics" → "pairs a visual animation with a sonification of the same underlying physics"
- Asteroids "About this simulation": "turns every asteroid into a single **musical** note" → "turns every asteroid into a single tone"

**Other locations to check:**
- `demo_html.wl` — intro strings and appMeta (source of the above)
- Root `README.md` — scan for "musical"
- `RELEASE_NOTES_v1.1.0.md` — scan for "musical"
- Each app's `README.md` — particularly signal, pendulum, lorenz, asteroids

## images/ app — post-enhancement items

### 3. demo_html.wl — images/ section needs updating

**Issue:** The demo HTML was generated before the images/ enhancements. The app description, listening guide, and audio label in `demo_html.wl`'s `appMeta` for the images entry no longer fully reflect the new modes (scan_horizontal, updated spectral colour palette, hsb timbre channel) or the existence of LISTENING_GUIDE.md.

**Fix:** Update the `images` entry in `demo_html.wl` appMeta:
- Description: mention the spectral colour-to-pitch mapping and the Hilbert vs scan_horizontal pedagogical sequence
- Listening guide: reference the spectral palette ("violet is the lowest pitch, red is the highest")
- Add a link to `images/LISTENING_GUIDE.md` in the "Run it yourself" section
- Audio label: update to "Listen — Hilbert curve brightness scan (log scale)" per item 1 above

### 4. demo.wl — consider scan_horizontal as second images demo preset

**Issue:** demo.wl currently runs images/ in brightness mode only. The scan_horizontal → brightness pedagogical sequence is now the recommended listening approach per LISTENING_GUIDE.md, but the demo only demonstrates one of the two.

**Decision needed:** Should demo.wl run images/ twice (scan_horizontal then brightness on the same test image) to make the Hilbert curve benefit directly audible? This adds ~30 seconds to demo runtime. Alternative: keep demo.wl as-is and rely on LISTENING_GUIDE.md. Recommend discussing before next release.

### 5. cellular/ app — note-holding enhancement (future targeted pass)

**Issue:** The `cellular` app maps population to pitch at each timestep, producing continuous notes even during stable periods. Rao's run-length encoding principle (hold a note during uniform runs, articulate only on change) would make population events significantly more audible — stable periods would sound stable, explosions would be clearly marked.

**Fix:** In a future targeted pass, adapt `cellular/src/sonify.wl` to hold pitch during stable-population periods and only articulate when population changes by more than a configurable threshold.

**Scope:** cellular/ only, one targeted Claude Code session.

## Resolved in v1.2.0 patch (post-tag)

### Item 5 resolved: cellular/ note-holding enhancement

**Fixed:** `cellular/src/sonify.wl` now uses run-length articulation with relative threshold (default 3%). Stable periods produce sustained tones; population changes produce new notes. Both Game of Life and Rule 110 modes updated. EventLayer accent tones preserved. CSV gains `articulated` and `run_length` columns. Config keys added: `articulation_mode`, `articulation_threshold`, `articulation_threshold_abs`, `base_note_duration`.

**Note:** This was implemented after the v1.2.0 tag. Should be included in the next consolidation pass and release notes for v1.3.0.
